name: Monolith
finish: Fine matte black polymer; vermilion mute button
route: Waveshare prototype; 40 mm round speaker upgrade
cost: Approx. $36-$44 prototype parts with upgraded speaker
description: The strongest first version: a small permanent shrine to one song. The taller body leaves room for the screen module above a round speaker. Thin USB power leaves the rear at shelf level.
risk: Listening quality, bass and actual current draw remain untested. Black case is a visual material study, not a manufactured finish.

name: Cube
route: Waveshare module; 40 x 20 mm slim speaker
cost: Approx. $37-$46 prototype parts with slim speaker
description: The most sculptural shape. A deep, quiet object with a compact face and one button. The slim speaker fits below the module; extra depth can hold an isolated acoustic chamber and ballast.
risk: Extra depth buys acoustic volume, not proven bass. A round 40 mm front driver needs a revised vertical layout.

name: Horizon
finish: Warm ivory textured polymer; vermilion button
cost: Custom baseline around $31 before freight and contingency
description: A small shelf radio reduced to one song. Screen and speaker sit side by side, giving the sound a direct path forward. Two-color amber imagery can be changed per edition in the media conversion.
risk: Requires custom electronics. The illustrated 2.4-inch screen is smaller than the Waveshare 2.8-inch prototype.

name: Timber
finish: Walnut appearance; dark inset baffle and woven grille
route: Waveshare module; slim speaker; wood outer sleeve
cost: Above the $30 target; wood fabrication not quoted
description: A warmer keepsake: a dark video window held in a wood cabinet. A printed acoustic inner enclosure would sit inside a wood sleeve, so the outer material is free to carry the collectible character.
risk: Wood machining and fabric application add labour. This is a premium material exploration, not a sourced enclosure.

name: Solar Wedge
display: 2.8-inch TFT; real 113 x 66 mm P124 solar envelope
route: Waveshare, P124, power-path charger, cell and 5 V boost
description: A visible study of the solar ambition. The sloped top fits the actual panel footprint, with the mute button on the right side. Solar supplements the battery in good sunlight; USB backup remains at the rear.
risk: Not self-sustaining on a normal indoor shelf. Charging, boost losses, temperature sensing and protected-cell integration need engineering.

name: Plinth
finish: Terracotta-textured polymer; warm metal button; dark base
route: Custom 2.4-inch board; slim speaker; wired contact base
cost: Custom baseline plus an unquoted dock, roughly $4-$8 extra
description: The cable belongs to the small display stand. The object receives low-voltage power through concealed underside contacts and remains battery-free. Its ceramic appearance is simulated in polymer to control cost.
risk: The base still has a wire. Lifting the object stops playback without a battery or hold-up circuit. Dock contacts and stability are not engineered.
